plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 4-date timeline completes: Mar 1894 & 1901 (George Oliver & Edward Schäfer discover adrenal blood-pressure surge at UCL; Jokichi Takamine & Keizo Uenaka crystallise pure adrenaline) · 16 Jan 1902 (William Bayliss & Ernest Starling sever every nerve to a jejunal loop at UCL and prove acid releases the blood-borne chemical messenger secretin) · 20 Jun 1905 (Ernest Starling coins the word 'hormone' from Greek hormōn, 'to set in motion', in his Croonian Lecture) · 1914–1977 (Edward Kendall isolates thyroxine & cortisone; Banting & Best isolate insulin; Rosalyn Yalow invents radioimmunoassay and Guillemin & Schally map brain-pituitary neuroendocrine control).

teach_overlay.scale: from a single afternoon nerve-cutting experiment in London to over fifty known human hormones, Bayliss and Starling revealed the wireless chemical postal service that runs your body
